## Summary

Implemented `householdId` assignment for the shares-household rule on `POST /api/owners`, keeping structural impact low by adding one small, self-contained function class rather than growing any existing class.

**New behaviour** — when a request sets `sharesHousehold: true`, the owner is allowed at an address already used by a same-lastName owner (this skip already existed), and now both the new owner and the existing household member are assigned the same stable `householdId`, which is returned on the owner.

**Files touched (6):**

1. **`AssignHousehold.java`** (new) — the whole behaviour lives here as one cohesive unit. When `sharesHousehold` is true it derives a deterministic, stable `HH-<12 hex>` id from the household's normalized last name + address (SHA-256), sets it on the new owner, and back-fills the same id onto any existing household member lacking one. Deterministic derivation guarantees every joiner gets an identical, non-blank id. Style mirrors the existing `EnsureUniqueHousehold`.
2. **`owners.POST.yml`** — inserted an `assignHousehold` step between `ensureUniqueHousehold` and `assignCode`, under the same transaction governance.
3. **`Owner.java`** — added the persisted `householdId` field + getter/setter, paralleling the existing `customerCode` field.
4. **`openapi.yml`** — added a read-only `householdId` string to the `Owner` schema, so the generated `OwnerDto` exposes it (MapStruct maps it by name automatically — no mapper change needed).
5. **`db/hsqldb/schema.sql`** — added the `household_id` column (hsqldb is the canonical, tested schema; the h2/postgres/mysql schemas are already stale, missing even `customer_code`, so I followed that precedent).
6. **`db/hsqldb/data.sql`** — added the trailing `NULL` the positional seed inserts needed for the new column.

I did not touch the existing pipeline functions or the mapper — the new logic is isolated to a fresh class, so no high-complexity class was edited.
